samples.claim: covering_fields repeated int32=11 lists co-located values. Under bit 13 it is independent of fields and can overlap; maintenance dependencies are their union. In legacy form covering entries are a trailing fields suffix in emission order, including a second appearance if also a key. Empty means no extra-column declaration. Critically, declarations do not prove payload availability: actual segment storage schema is authoritative; readers must verify the column exists or fall back to base-table take. Maintenance may legally withdraw payload while retaining declaration; that state is not corruption.
samples.evidence:
362 |   /* The fields whose values this index co-locates alongside its own data, so a
363 |    * query projecting only those columns can be answered from the index without
364 |    * a take against the base table.
365 |    *
366 |    * When the manifest has feature flag 1 << 13, this declaration is independent
367 |    * of `fields` and has no positional relationship to it. A field may occur in
368 |    * both lists when the index carries a value it is also keyed on. Consumers
369 |    * must use the union of `fields` and `covering_fields` as the index dependency
370 |    * set.
371 |    *
372 |    * Without feature flag 1 << 13, the legacy contract applies: the carried columns
373 |    * form the trailing suffix of `fields` in emission order. A column the
374 |    * index is both keyed on and carries appears twice, once as a key and once in
375 |    * the carried suffix.
376 |    *
377 |    * Empty for an index that carries no extra columns, which is every index
378 |    * written before this field existed.
379 |    *
380 |    * This declaration is not authoritative for what the segment can actually
381 |    * serve. The segment's own storage schema is: a reader must confirm the
382 |    * storage carries a column before answering a query from it, and fall back to
383 |    * a take against the base table otherwise. A declaration naming columns the
384 |    * storage does not hold is a legal state, not corruption -- a maintenance
385 |    * operation that cannot carry the values through a rebuild is permitted to
386 |    * withdraw the payload while leaving this declaration in place.
387 |    */
388 |   repeated int32 covering_fields = 11;
389 | }

samples.claim: reader_feature_flags uint64 tag 9 requires rejection when any set bit is unrecognized. The comment lists bit 0 deletions, 1 stable row IDs, 2 deprecated v2 indicator, 3 table config, 4 multiple bases, 5 disabled transaction-file writes, 6 overlays, 7 covering columns. Without bit 13, covering columns are the trailing fields suffix. Both readers and writers must reject unknown covering semantics to avoid querying/maintaining an index as if merely carried columns were indexed keys.
samples.evidence:
116 |   /* Feature flags for readers.
117 |    *
118 |    * A bitmap of flags that indicate which features are required to be able to
119 |    * read the table. If a reader does not recognize a flag that is set, it
120 |    * should not attempt to read the dataset.
121 |    *
122 |    * Known flags:
123 |    * * 1 << 0: deletion files are present
124 |    * * 1 << 1: row ids are stable and stored as part of the fragment metadata.
125 |    * * 1 << 2: use v2 format (deprecated)
126 |    * * 1 << 3: table config is present
127 |    * * 1 << 4: dataset uses multiple base paths
128 |    * * 1 << 5: transaction file writes are disabled
129 |    * * 1 << 6: data overlay files are present (see DataOverlayFile). Readers that do
130 |    *   not understand overlays must refuse the dataset, since ignoring an overlay
131 |    *   would silently return stale base values.
132 |    * * 1 << 7: some index declares covering columns. Without 1 << 13,
133 |    *   the carried columns form the trailing suffix of IndexMetadata.fields in
134 |    *   emission order (see IndexMetadata). Readers
135 |    *   that do not understand covering columns must refuse the dataset, since
136 |    *   selecting an index by membership of fields would answer a query on a
137 |    *   merely-carried column with an index keyed on a different column. Writers
138 |    *   must refuse it too: one that treats every entry of fields as keyed would
139 |    *   maintain the index against the wrong dependency set.
samples.review_note: The protobuf reader-flag comment explicitly lists bits0..7 and requires refusal for unknown covering semantics, including writers avoiding incorrect dependency maintenance. This sampled slice documents comments, not runtime enforcement.

samples.claim: From<&Schema> for Fields flattens each top-level field subtree in order. From<&Schema> for FieldsWithMeta uses that flattening and clones the entire string metadata map before consuming values into bytes. Neither assigns IDs nor validates the input; there is no fallible result.
samples.review_note: Both Schema conversions are infallible locally: flatten roots in order, clone metadata strings, then consume values into bytes. No ID assignment or input validation is added.

samples.claim: FIFO topological walk takes each transition once (otherwise explicit visited-twice corruption), appends it, decrements every outgoing edge count and queues when zero. Any unvisited records at end mean cycle. Independent roots preserve serialized relative order; newly ready nodes append behind already-ready nodes, so this is not a global sort by dataset_version or fragment ID. Local counters use ordinary arithmetic justified by constructed graph, not checked arithmetic.
samples.review_note: Fresh traversal takes transitions once, decrements incoming edges, queues at zero and checks final count. Supplemental VecDeque construction preserves serialized root order and pop_front/push_back establish FIFO rather than global version sorting.

samples.claim: Full-span synthetic bitmap-cost fixture compares bitmap estimate with saturated holes and requires bitmap cost<usizeMAX. Its comment explicitly assumes64-bit; no target-width cfg guards the test. On32-bit that estimate would saturate too, so this assertion is not portable as written; source deduction only, no32-bit execution.
samples.review_note: Fresh synthetic test lacks a target-width guard. Supplemental formula uses24+ceil(2^64/8) in u128 and saturating usize conversion, confirming the32-bit non-portability inference without executing on32-bit.

samples.claim: Crate-visible state.extend_range appends to caller Vec. Non-bitmap Range clips selection.end to segment length and extends base-adjusted interval if start<end; Ranges clamps both ordinals to u32MAX and delegates runs.extend_values; other variants loop every requested ordinal and filter_map get, omitting out-of-bounds entries. Non-bitmap calls leave bitmap scan state untouched. Empty/reversed selections append nothing on valid state; no Result or reserve.
samples.review_note: Fresh non-bitmap extend_range branches clip Range, clamp Ranges to u32MAX and filter_map other ordinals. They return before bitmap state updates, with no Result or reserve.

samples.claim: Public decode requests full range, take clones the UInt32Array selector and forwards it, and get forwards arbitrary convertible ReadBatchParams. All converge on decode_impl without another validation layer. No cache, value dictionary merge or independently optimized take is introduced.
samples.review_note: Fresh decode/take/get methods all forward to decode_impl; take clones the selector and decode uses full range. There is no additional validation, cache or dictionary merge in these wrappers.

samples.claim: Private probe returns None for zero fragments or no start <= row ID. partition_point finds the candidate upper bound. An iterative stackless left-to-right DFS uses max-end tree values to prune subtrees, tests FragmentEntry::resolve at leaves, and continues after the first live hit to detect a second. Two hits return Internal naming the row ID. Ascending from right children adjusts lo/width; reaching root ends the walk, while lo>=upper terminates remaining sorted starts. No recursion or heap stack per lookup; worst work depends on overlapping envelopes and segment searches, not solely one binary search.
samples.review_note: Fresh probe handles empty/no-start cases, uses partition_point then a stackless max-end-pruned traversal, and reports a second live fragment as Internal. It continues after a first hit; complexity includes envelope overlap and leaf resolution.
